data.name: Ansharah
data.gender_notes: Ansharah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'anshara', meaning to support or help. In Islamic history, Ansharah is a name given to those who provide assistance and support to others, embodying the spirit of kindness and compassion. The name Ansharah carries the meaning “Support, Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ansharah usually hope their child will grow to embody support, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ansharah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Support, Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ansharah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Ansharah comes from the Arabic root 'anshar', which means to be blessed with good fortune and prosperity, and to be close to God. It is a name that has been associated with the prophets and is considered to be a means of seeking protection and refuge from God. The name Ansharah is also believed to bring good fortune and prosperity to those who bear it, and to bring the bearer closer to God. In Islamic tradition, the name Ansharah is considered to be a blessing and a source of spiritual guidance, and is often recited as a form of dhikr or remembrance of God.

historical_references.reference: Ansharah were a pre-Islamic Arab tribe who are believed to have lived in the region of the Arabian Peninsula known as Najd. They were known for their fierce warriors and were a significant power in central Arabia during the pre-Islamic period.
historical_references.context: Ansharah were mentioned in several pre-Islamic Arabic poems and were known to have had conflicts with other tribes, including the Quraysh, who later became the tribe of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

historical_references.reference: Ansharah also played a role in early Islamic history when they joined the army of the first Islamic caliph, Abu Bakr, during the Ridda Wars (632-633 CE). The Ridda Wars were a series of military campaigns launched by Abu Bakr to suppress rebellions in Arabian Peninsula after the death of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).
historical_references.context: Ansharah joined the Islamic army as a significant contingent and played a crucial role in the Battle of Dumat al-Jandal, which was a turning point in the Ridda Wars. The defeat of the Ansharah forces marked the end of major resistance to the early Islamic state.
